new_statements.quote: 1.4. A sílaba tônica é sempre a última da palavra. [pa'di] 'tamanduá' [da'pra] 'pé' [pse'di] 'é bom'. Nos casos onde a vogal final se perde ou está em processo de se perder, a sílaba tônica é a nova sílaba última. [mãto watÍ'brÍ] ou [mãto wa'tÍbr] 'ele saiu' [kuta'bi] 'realmente' [kutabi + di] ––> [ku'tabÊdÊ] 'é real'
new_statements.translation: 1.4. The stressed syllable is always the last one of the word. [pa'di] 'anteater' [da'pra] 'foot' [pse'di] 'is good'. In cases where the final vowel is lost or is in the process of being lost, the stressed syllable is the new last syllable. [mãto watÍ'brÍ] or [mãto wa'tÍbr] 'he went out' [kuta'bi] 'really' [kutabi + di] --> [ku'tabÊdÊ] 'is real'
new_statements.citation: Mattos, Rinaldo de (1971). Fonêmica Xerente. Série Lingüística N 1. Brasília. pp. 79-100.
new_statements.locator: §1.4 'A sílaba tônica', p. 2 of the SIL 2003 web re-edition ('SL-1 Xerente ', 15 pp.); original Série Lingüística pagination (pp. 79-100) not recoverable from this copy. Souza (2008) cites the same passage as 'Mattos (1973, p. 2)'.
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (extracted text, 15 pp., text layer present). §1.4 is on PDF p. 2, lines: '1.4. A sílaba tônica é sempre a última da palavra. [mãto watÍ'brÍ] ou [mãto wa'tÍbr] 'ele saiu' [kuta'bi] 'realmente'' — then the page-2 footer, and the last example '[kutabi + di] ––> [ku'tabÊdÊ] 'é real'' sits at the top of PDF p. 3 (the reader's 'p. 2' locator is right for the rule sentence; only the final example spills onto p. 3). The quote otherwise matches character for character. A a full-text search for stress/accent the whole text for tôni…
new_statements.relation_note: Catalog record (our earlier survey-2026-08-31) gives final stress = fixed final; Mattos states exactly that ('sempre a última da palavra'). This work is the primary source that Souza 2008, Cotrim 2016 and Grannier 2010 all cite for the final-stress rule.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the final syllable of the word, without exception; when a word-final vowel has been lost (the language is undergoing extensive vowel loss), stress moves to the syllable that has become the new final syllable. Stress is predictable and not marked in the phonemic transcription.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated as exceptions. The vowel-loss cases are presented as the same rule applied to the new final syllable; in the example [kutabi + di] -> [ku'tabÊdÊ] the stress surfaces on the syllable before the non-phonemic transitional vowels [Ê], i.e. on the syllable that is phonemically final after the loss of /i/.
new_statements.identity_note: Mattos describes the Xerente spoken in seven villages between the Tocantins and Sono rivers (then Goiás, now Tocantins), data 1964-1966, main consultant Anjo dos Santos; ~500 speakers at the time. No dialect split is discussed; this is the same variety (Akwẽ-Xerente) treated in all later work. The Xavante comparison in §1 concerns the sister language, not a Xerente dialect.
